name: Snake equation
summary: A cup followed by a cap is a straight wire.
description:
The snake (or yanking) equations say that the cup and the cap are each other's inverse when composed side by side: a wire with a zigzag can be pulled straight. They are the defining axioms of a compact closed category, and hold in the ZX-, ZH- and ZW-calculus alike. Hadzihasanovic's presentation of the ZW-calculus lists them as axiom $adj_L$ (and its mirror image).

Together with [cups as spiders](../cup-as-spider/) this is what makes *only connectivity matters* work. In PyZX and ZXLive it holds by construction.
unchecked_reason: bare cups and caps cannot be represented with ZXLive-style boundaries

source.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $adj_L$
